proof_judgments.P2 / v13-c02-envelopes: The fixed feasible target set gives price concavity, degree-one expenditure and every minimizer’s supergradient inequality. A common positive price bound controls nearby optimizers; closed feasibility makes their cluster points optimal. Uniqueness gives a full vector derivative, while compact H gives the directional minimum. Roy uses both signs of a feasible income-price perturbation and divides only under positive income derivative.
proof_judgments.P3 / v13-c02-slutsky: The row-demand/column-price convention gives Dp x + xm x-transpose. A C1 Hicksian gradient makes the expenditure potential C2, yielding symmetry and a negative-semidefinite Hessian with the price null direction. The skew share field satisfies the preliminary checks but violates this necessary smooth symmetry; no generic global sufficiency or nonsmooth impossibility theorem is inferred.
proof_judgments.P4 / v13-c02-integrability: Positive C1 concave degree-one c and its nonnegative gradient give Euler and a full-price supporting inequality. The infimum-defined U is finite, concave, monotone and homogeneous. Explicit nonnegative witnesses establish target and income attainment without assuming boundary continuity or arbitrary uniqueness. The concrete min index is proved with positive-price limits including zero coordinates; AM–GM separately proves its unique Hicksian demand.
proof_judgments.P5 / v13-c02-producer: Supremum/infimum signs yield profit convexity and cost-price concavity. The profit envelope retains closedness, nearby finite attainment, bounded optimizers and uniqueness. The repaired conditional-cost statement now likewise retains closedness of the feasible input set. Output convexity requires a separate feasible-plan mixing condition. Model AM–GM and completed-square bounds prove global optima; the full Hessian square identity and r=0 qualification are correct.
proof_judgments.P6 / v13-c02-reconstruction: Affine-dependence elimination proves that at most L+1 generators suffice and therefore the convex hull is compact. Its disposal hull is closed by subsequences. A strict separator cannot have a negative coordinate under free disposal; compact support permits a small positive perturbation that retains the gap. This reconstructs the convex disposal hull using all positive prices, while preserving the original nonconvex and tie-supply identification limits.

resolved_findings.issue: Attainment, locally bounded optimizers and uniqueness alone do not preserve feasibility of optimizer limits when the input set is not closed.
resolved_findings.witness: Z={(2,1)} union {(1−t,2+t+t²):0<t≤1/2}. At p=(1,1), (2,1) uniquely minimizes. All nearby optima are bounded and attained. For p1≤p2, C=2p1+p2; for p1>p2, C=p1+2p2−(p1−p2)²/(4p2), attained at t=(p1−p2)/(2p2). The p1 derivative limits are 2 and 1. The missing limit input is (1,2).
